Where this node goes live in the one cut-over order of the book

section.title: Purpose
section.s: N-25 is the one writer of the GitHub commit status coq/gate on a head sha: success when every planned unit passed, failure when a unit failed, error when the infrastructure ran out or a newer head superseded the run; with the required status check on main (D05, ruling C43) GitHub itself refuses a merge without a green gate, and an agent can read the verdict but never edit it; only the coq-gate GitHub App writes the context, and the required check names its app_id, so no other writer can satisfy it (shared/authority.xml#github-app).
It closes the loop the investigation found open: no status had ever been posted, main required no check, and the only gate was a script reading records (RC3 item 7, RC7, L07 section 5 item 3).

Input to output: the set of pod.run records (N-24) and check.verdict records (N-46) for one head sha and plan attempt starts it; the posted status plus a gate.run record ends it; N-04 sees the status on its next poll and N-08 reads the verdict from the snapshot.

section.title: Input records: pod.run and check.verdict for one head sha

record.s: The node reads the newest suite.plan (or main.plan) for the head sha and attempt, and the result record per entry: pod.run for kind pod (N-24), check.verdict for kind spec-check (N-46); the input is complete when every entry has a result record or the plan's bound has passed.
record.field: The pull request or 0 for main.
name, kind, code, outcome, log and the per-test outcomes per entry.
The rows of tests/expected-red.json (planned) at the head sha that apply (record.schema.json#/$defs/expected_red_row), possibly empty.

section.title: Output: the coq/gate commit status and the gate.run record
section.s: The status: POST /repos/jkkelley/coq-jev-herdr-plugin/statuses/<head_sha> with context coq/gate, state pending while the plan runs, then success, failure or error, a description of at most 140 characters (N pods passed; <unit> failed plus K more; infrastructure failed after the ladder: <reason>; superseded by <sha12>; plan refused: <reason>), and target_url the gate page link.

record.field: The attempt whose results this verdict is from.
pass, fail, timeout, infra, superseded, spec_check_pass, spec_check_fail, expected_red.
name and log of the unit the description names.
GitHub status id, created_at, the app_id that created it, and attempts used to post.

section.s: The gate page link: the Jenkins build page of the plan's build (http://${SITE_JENKINS_HOST}/job/coq-gate/N/, the host from the owner's site file) which holds every unit log and is reachable on the owner's LAN and tailnet; the bearings page (N-32) also shows the gate.run record per pull request, and the map's machine screen (N-39) links both.

section.title: Mechanism: the verdict rule, the status post, the page link, supersession, the required check
section.step: When N-23 or N-26 writes the plan with a build number, this node posts coq/gate pending with description "running N units" (an outbox effect, operation key N-25/status.post/<sha>@coq/gate@<plan_attempt>/r1 with state pending in the request hash); when a plan is refused (412) it posts error with the refusal's reason, so the worker sees why there is no run.

The verdict rule, pure over the result set (finish() of coqGate.groovy, moved into the Go service): any result with outcome infra or code 500 and no later successful attempt available means error; else any fail, timeout or check fail means failure, and the description names the first failing unit by plan order plus the count of the rest; else every entry has a pass and the state is success with the pod count; a result set with a superseded unit is error superseded; an empty plan (nothing to run) is success "nothing to run".

The expected-red manifest (F19): tests/expected-red.json (planned) at the head sha lists tests that must fail, each with test_ref (path, test_id, content_sha256), the ticket and expected_failure (kind, match) taken from the ticket's acceptance (nodes/N-17/spec.xml); a row is honoured only when the test file's sha256 equals content_sha256 and, for a row this head adds, when it equals an acceptance test_ref of the head's ticket (ticket A lands the test and its row). A listed test that fails with a matching failure counts expected_red and does not make the gate red; a listed test that fails otherwise is failure (wrong failure reason); a listed test that passes is failure "unexpected pass: remove the row" (ticket B flips the code and removes the row in one head); a unit whose runner reported no per-test outcomes cannot prove an expected failure and counts as fail.

Error from infrastructure is not final at once: the gate run has plan-attempt tries (shared/retry-budget.xml#layers, max 2); on infra the node asks N-23 (or N-26) to plan attempt 2, a fresh build with its own operation key, and the status stays pending with "retrying attempt 2"; after attempt 2's infra the status is error and one card is posted by N-28 (dedupe key node:N-25:head_sha); the gate phase is never re-dispatched after that (gate-phase layer, max 1).

The post: the verdict's Commit writes gate.run and the effects row of operation status.post (shared/retry-budget.xml#operations) together; the outbox worker posts with an installation token of the coq-gate GitHub App (shared/authority.xml#credential-matrix row coq-gate), 10 s timeout per call, retried only by the status-post layer; before any repost it reads GET /repos/jkkelley/coq-jev-herdr-plugin/commits/<sha>/statuses for context coq/gate created by that app, and equal state and description is done (the read-back, never the snapshot); the status id and app id go into gate.run posted.

Supersession: N-07's tick compares each open pull request's head in forge.snapshot with the newest plan; when the head moved, N-07 writes plan.superseded 410 for the old sha, the Go service stops the old build, and this node posts error "superseded by <new sha12>" on the old sha, so no sha is ever left pending (the abortPrevious semantic of the old Jenkinsfile, now owned by the scheduler).

The required check: branch protection on main requires context coq/gate with app_id forge.gate_app_id and strict true, applied once by the owner with forge-admin (shared/authority.xml#github-app); this node never applies or removes protection. The protection check is this node's and read-only: at service start and on the daily tick it reads GET /repos/jkkelley/coq-jev-herdr-plugin/branches/main/protection with forge-read and asserts strict true, a check entry coq/gate with that app_id, linear history and no force pushes; it writes protection.observed 200 (config hash, observed_at) when all hold and protection.drift 412 naming each difference with one card otherwise; N-09 reads them.
gate.run is the derived notification and the audit trail; the authority is the status on GitHub (D05), which N-08 reads from forge.snapshot; no node reads gate.run in place of the status.
section.mermaid: flowchart LR P[plan with build number] --> S0[post coq/gate pending] R[every entry has a pod.run or check.verdict] --> V{verdict rule} V -- all pass --> OK[post success; gate.run 201] V -- a fail or timeout --> F[post failure naming the unit; gate.run 422] V -- infra on attempt 1 --> A[plan attempt 2; pending] V -- infra on attempt 2 --> E[post error; gate.run 500; one card] N[newer head on the same PR] --> X[stop old build; post error superseded; gate.run 410] OK --> N04[N-04 poll sees the status] F --> N04 E --> N04 X --> N04 N04 --> N08[N-08 gate check reads the verdict]
section.s: The merge path after this node: N-08 reads green, N-19's review.passed lands on the same head, N-09 merges by machine (D15, ruling C50); GitHub enforces the check independently of every record.

section.title: How it starts without an agent typing
section.s: N-07 dispatches the verdict as a system job under the plan's lease when every entry of a plan attempt has a result record, or when the plan's bound has passed (then the missing results are infra, N-24 section waits w6); the comparison is level-triggered, so a result that arrives late or a crash before the post is settled on the next tick.
The pending post is dispatched by the same rule the moment a plan has a build number.
At service start, every plan with results and no gate.run of the same attempt is re-evaluated; a status already on GitHub is read from the snapshot and not re-posted.

section.title: Every wait, its timeout and its fallback

wait.timeout: retry-budget.xml#deadlines d-plan-attempt per attempt; the whole gate run within d-gate-run.
wait.fallback: Missing results become infra (N-24 writes them with reason result-missing); the verdict rule runs on what exists; attempts and the card as in section retries.

wait.on: GitHub answering the status POST from the coq-gate App.
wait.timeout: 10 s per call; the status-post layer (shared/retry-budget.xml#layers) bounds the tries and #deadlines d-status-post the whole post.
wait.fallback: An unknown outcome is looked up by the statuses read before any repost; after the last try status.post.failed 500 with the head sha and one card; gate.run stays with posted.ok false.

wait.on: The old build stopping on supersession.
wait.timeout: 60 s for POST /stop to take effect, polled on the build's building flag.
wait.fallback: The status on the old sha is posted regardless; a build that keeps running ends on its own bound and its results are written as superseded 410 and ignored.

section.title: Retries, recovery and the report
section.s: Infrastructure results re-trigger the plan once (plan-attempt max 2; the pod ladder inside each attempt is the inner layer and retries pod failures only); test failures never re-trigger anything.

The post is retried by the status-post layer alone (max 3 tries in all, never per tick), each preceded by the statuses read-back, then status.post.failed and one card; nothing loops, because the operation key makes every retry the same post.

After the second plan attempt's infra the status is error with the reason and one card; the pull request stays red until a new head; the worker lane sees the reason on the pull request and in the record.
Recovery after a crash: records and the GitHub status are the only state; the start comparison re-posts what is missing and skips what is present.

section.title: Many agents at once
section.s: One writer: only the coq-gate GitHub App can post a status that satisfies the required check (app_id), and only coq-svc holds its key; seats hold no forge credential and cannot reach the forge (shared/authority.xml#seat-isolation) and the reviewer reads gh pr checks; a seat cannot post, edit or delete a status, which is the T04 property the field calls a verdict the agent reads and cannot change.

Many heads at once: statuses are per sha and the key includes the sha and attempt; two pull requests never share a status; two attempts of one sha post in attempt order because the verdict job holds the plan lease.
Two Go service instances: the lease's fencing token; the loser's gate.run commit is 412 stale_token, so no effects row of its own exists and nothing is posted.

A seat that pushes while the gate runs: the new head is planned, the old run is superseded and says so on the old sha; the reviewer reading the pull request sees pending on the new head and never a stale green.

The reviewer and the gate on one head: review.passed and coq/gate are independent records on the same sha; N-09 requires both; neither waits on the other, so a review posted before green simply waits in the store.
Collision answer in one line: single status writer with a lease per plan, content-keyed idempotent posts, per-sha statuses, supersession owned by the scheduler, 409 on a stale writer.

section.title: Status codes this node emits
section.emits: The status pending was posted; nobody acts.
coq/gate success; N-08 reads green; N-09 may merge with review.passed.
coq/gate failure; the worker lane acts on the named unit's log; a new head re-enters.
coq/gate error after the last plan attempt; N-28 posts one card.
coq/gate error plan refused (fork, no image, planner error); the worker lane acts.
Main's protection matches; N-09 reads the newest as its precondition.
Protection differs from the expected configuration; one card; N-09 holds merges while it is the newest.
The coq/gate post failed after the status-post layer; one card; the head stays without a terminal status until the next post succeeds.

section.title: State paths and the cleanup script for each
section.path: The verdict input set and the post request and response bodies, for audit.

path.cleanup: kept on purpose: GitHub keeps statuses with the commit; nothing to delete, and a status is never edited after a terminal state

section.path: Not a host path; listed so the rule holds.

path.cleanup: none: applied and removed only by the owner with forge-admin (shared/authority.xml#github-app); this node holds no credential that can change it

section.s: The script dry-runs by default, acts with --apply, retries 3 times and exits 4 listing what remains; N-45 registers it.

section.title: DAG edges in and out
section.out: The posted status appears in the next forge.snapshot.

item.check: coq/gate is a required status check on main with strict true and app_id forge.gate_app_id.
item.proof: The newest protection.observed 200 of this node names the context and the app id (not-run).

item.check: A listed expected-red test failing as expected keeps the gate green; the same test passing turns it red.
item.proof: Verdict rule fixtures expected-red-hit, expected-red-wrong-reason, unexpected-pass, row-added-without-acceptance (not-run).

item.check: Every planned head ends with a terminal status: no sha stays pending past its bound.
item.proof: A daily query over forge.snapshot: zero heads with coq/gate pending older than PT3H; the alert in section monitoring.

item.check: The verdict rule is pure and tested: success, first failure named, infra error, superseded, empty plan.
item.proof: Go unit tests in the service package for the rule with the five fixtures; go test exit 0 in the scheduler suite's pod.run.

item.check: A post is idempotent on content.
item.proof: Scenario repost in the fake forge: two verdict runs on one result set produce one status.

item.check: A newer head supersedes the old run and the old sha reads error superseded.
item.proof: Scenario supersede: old sha status error with the new sha12 in the description; the old build's stop was called.

item.check: No seat holds a credential that can post a status, and a status from any writer other than the coq-gate App does not satisfy the required check.
item.proof: shared/authority.xml#credential-matrix has no seat row for a forge credential; a test status posted with forge-read-like scope is ignored by protection (not-run).

item.check: The target_url opens the build with the unit logs.
item.proof: A GET on the target_url from the tailnet returns 200 and lists units/*.log.

item.check: The first live pull request after cut-over carries a coq/gate status.
item.proof: gh pr checks on that pull request shows coq/gate with a state; the gate.run record id in the ledger.

section.title: Permissions
section.s: The Go service (coq-svc): the coq-gate GitHub App key, whose installation token has commit statuses write only, for the post; forge-read for the statuses read-back and the protection read (shared/authority.xml#credential-matrix); no administration write credential.
Jenkins: no GitHub credential for the gate; Jenkins posts nothing to GitHub (shared/authority.xml#credential-matrix row jenkins-held covers only the image and map pipelines).
Seats: no forge credential and no route to the forge (shared/authority.xml#seat-isolation); the verdict reaches them in their brief and in records.

The owner: branch protection is applied, changed or removed only with forge-admin from the owner's keyring as break glass; protection.drift reports any change and carries one card until protection is back.

section.title: Monitoring
section.s: Status fields: pending heads and their age, verdicts by state in the last 24 h, post failures, attempts used per head, time from pr.opened to a terminal status (p50 and p95), protection state.
Alerts (N-41): a head pending past its bound; status.post.failed; protection.failed or the context missing; verdict error rate above 10 percent in a day (infrastructure trouble).
Map: N-25 is the lamp on every pull request item on the belt; the stats screen shows time-to-verdict.

section.title: Runbook
section.step: A red pull request: the description names the unit; the log is behind the target_url and in the pod.run record; the fix is a new commit, which replans; nobody re-runs a failed assertion.
An error status: superseded needs nothing; infrastructure after the ladder has a card; the N-24 runbook names the cause classes.
Protection drift: the protection.drift 412 card names what differs; the owner re-applies it with forge-admin (shared/authority.xml#github-app); this node changes nothing.
status.post.failed: the card names the GitHub error; once GitHub answers, the next verdict tick posts through a new effect after the statuses read-back.

section.title: Sources cited
